messages.question: Correction to my own round-1 tell (M2.7), which you caught and which I am propagating rather than quietly dropping: I stated CIEN's 'next-quarter guide $6.42bn vs $6.33bn consensus'. Per Ciena's release the $6.42bn is the RAISED FULL-YEAR FY26 guide; the FQ4 guide is $1.75bn +/- $50m. The read-through to LITE and COHR survives the correction and is arguably stronger on the corrected basis, because the load-bearing figure is not the guide at all -- it is backlog $8.5bn, up $800m sequentially, with book-to-bill well above 1. Backlog and book-to-bill are forward component demand; a full-year revenue guide is not. I accept your ambiguous-to-tailwind classification: the LITE/COHR lead-lag is the cluster playbook's claim and I found no company or analyst source tying CIEN backlog to LITE/COHR orders either.

answers_to_your_questions.answer: Held, and your answer is the reason it is held rather than upgraded. GLW stays my laggard and the ATM stays an unresolved overhang. I accept the correction to my own reorder condition: I had written 'a disclosure of ZERO usage moves GLW above CIEN', and you have shown that condition is not reachable through the 09-11 filings -- an ATM with no fixed price, no share count and no obligation to sell produces silence, and silence is not zero. I am rewriting that condition to name the document that can actually settle it: the Q3 10-Q segment/equity note quantifying shares sold under the programme, expected around the 2026-10-27 Q3 print. Until then GLW's laggard rank rests on two independent legs, and I want it on record that only one of them is the ATM: the other is stack position -- passive fiber and specialty glass carry no active-component content and sit at the node the margin pool is migrating away from, which would rank GLW last in this cluster even if the ATM were cancelled tomorrow. The genuine case against my own call is unchanged and unaddressed by your answer: Q2 core EPS +30%, 19% sales CAGR guided through 2030, Q3 core sales guide $4.9-5.0bn intact, and the 09-18 +3% says the market has already discounted much of the dilution scare.
